name: Braille Hub
summary: Translate Persian and German text to Braille in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
description:
Braille Hub is an open-source accessibility platform for text and music workflows in Microsoft 365. The current release brings specification-driven Braille translation and Braille Music features into a single add-in while keeping the translation engines reusable outside Office.

For text workflows, Braille Hub supports Persian, German, and ordinary English/Latin spans. In Microsoft Word, a supported text selection can be translated, previewed as Unicode Braille, copied, replaced, or inserted after the current selection. In Microsoft Excel, the add-in works with one selected plain-text cell and allows the reviewed Braille result to replace that cell. In Microsoft PowerPoint, a selected text range can be translated and replaced after preview. Host-specific checks guard against stale selections or changed content before write-back.

The current English and Latin capability is uncontracted six-dot Braille. It does not claim UEB Grade 2 or contracted English Braille compliance. Persian translation remains specification-driven through the current fa-ir-g1 profile and shared runtime architecture. German Braille is available for Deutschland/Österreich and Schweiz with Basisschrift, Vollschrift, and Kurzschrift through the shared German Core/SDK runtime.

Braille Hub also provides Braille Music from Standard MIDI files in Microsoft Word. MIDI files are read locally in the task pane. The add-in detects available Track + Channel source lines, requires an explicit source-line choice when multiple lines are present, and generates both Unicode Music Braille and BRF / Braille ASCII projections. The exact successful preview can then be inserted at the current Word caret or selection. Unsupported musical material fails explicitly rather than being silently removed or simplified.

The Microsoft 365 integration does not contain a separate translation table. Word, Excel, and PowerPoint consume the same public SDK and reusable Core and Music engines used by the wider project. This architecture is intended to keep present and future integrations aligned with the same tested behavior.

Braille Hub is intended for users, educators, accessibility specialists, developers, researchers, and organizations preparing or evaluating accessible text and music. No publisher-controlled account, sign-in flow, analytics system, or cloud translation service is required by the current audited release. Supported translation processing runs through the client-side application architecture.

The current release is distributed free of charge as open-source software. The project Core, SDK, and supporting packages are released under the MIT License. Public support, privacy information, installation guidance, and end-user terms are provided through the project’s hosted documentation.
